judgments.rationale: The markscheme awards implicit differentiation and then the normal-line calculation from the gradient. The trigonometric expression is the context, not a trigonometry-topic method.

Maximizing the cone volume is the dominant method and is explicitly done by differentiation. The Pythagorean relation in triangle OXB is a distinct, credited geometric setup step.

These are all materially credited; the original Functions ownership is not.

The tree is a conditional probability model, and part (c) explicitly asks for the probability of passing the third paper given exactly one prior pass; the markscheme evaluates that conditional ratio. Conditional probability is therefore materially assessed alongside the tree model.

All marks concern graph structure: edge bounds, Eulerian circuits, planar graphs, face counting, and Euler’s formula. The supplied legacy Graph theory and algorithms skill is materially and directly assessed, rather than Counting and combinatorics.

The question and markscheme assess set difference, symmetric difference, and distributive/associative properties of set operations. The supplied legacy Sets, relations and groups skill is the direct owner.

The Cayley table, Latin-square property, identity and inverse, cyclicity, subgroup, and isomorphism are all group-theory methods. The supplied legacy Sets, relations and groups skill directly covers this content.

Cross products and parallel-vector reasoning earn vector-geometry marks, while most of the remaining work classifies relations and equivalence classes. Those two materially assessed areas are owned by Vectors, lines and planes and the supplied legacy Sets, relations and groups skill.

The marks prove uniqueness of a group identity and test associativity and identity for a custom binary operation. This is directly group/operation theory, owned by the supplied legacy Sets, relations and groups skill.

Hypothesis testing, p-value interpretation, correlation/regression validity, and the conclusion are statistical inference. The bivariate-normal assumption is supporting context, not a separately assessed normal-distribution calculation.

Bias and efficiency of estimators dominate part (a), while the negative-binomial and reciprocal-expectation work materially assesses discrete random variables and probability models. Binomial expansion is not used.
Confidence intervals, critical regions, Type I/II errors, and power-style parameter calculation are statistical inference; the normal sampling distribution is explicitly used throughout.
The negative-binomial PGF and sum distribution are discrete probability models, and part (b)(iii) explicitly asks for a conditional probability. No binomial expansion is assessed.
